questions.question: Explain why the Moon seems to change shape during the month.
questions.expected_answer: The Moon is always round, and the Sun always lights up the half that faces the Sun. As the Moon travels around the Earth, we see different amounts of that sunlit half. Sometimes we see none of it, sometimes a thin crescent, sometimes half, and sometimes all of it. These shapes are the phases of the Moon.

questions.question: Explain the difference between waxing and waning.
questions.expected_answer: When the Moon is waxing, the bright part we can see is growing bigger each night, from new Moon towards full Moon. When the Moon is waning, the bright part is getting smaller each night, from full Moon back towards new Moon.

questions.question: Name the main phases of the Moon in order, starting with the new Moon, and say how long the cycle takes.
questions.expected_answer: New Moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full Moon, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent, and then new Moon again. The whole cycle takes about twenty-nine and a half days.
